questions.q: What does the X plus Y equation illustrate?
a: Gains in one area of life cost time in another
Happiness can be calculated exactly
Money and success always rise together
Two people are needed to be happy
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the equation to explain tradeoffs between work and play.

questions.q: What risk does the summary attach to working 80-hour weeks?
a: Relationships suffer and you may end up alone
You earn less than those working 40 hours
Your health improves through discipline
You lose the chance of promotion
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns that constant work leaves little time for the people who matter.

questions.q: What should you do once you reach financial security?
a: Shift focus to enjoying freedom and relationships
Keep working harder to grow your savings
Retire as early as physically possible
Compare your wealth with your peers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the point of money is the freedom to work less and give more.

questions.q: Why did David Carey leave publishing at his peak?
a: He wanted to help young people, not fire friends
He had lost interest in earning money
He was offered a better job elsewhere
He wanted more time to travel
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses his choice as an example of stepping back to enjoy freedom.

questions.q: What does the summary say keeps a relationship strong?
a: Forgiveness, without keeping score of who did what
Regular grand gestures and expensive gifts
Agreeing on everything to avoid conflict
Splitting every responsibility exactly in half
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that competition and scorekeeping erode love.
